correctness.rationale: PASS. At equilibrium on an N-cycle, Kirchhoff balance forces identical sine currents J on every edge. A positive definite reduced Jacobian cannot have two nonpositive edges, and a single negative ordinary-unit edge is excluded by comparing its magnitude c with the (m−1)/c positive path resistance; consequently all m ordinary increments are the same acute α. The weak w<=wc=sin(3π/(2m)) bound excludes winding |q|>=2 and excludes an acute weak increment in the open range. For q=1, β∈(π/2,π), α=(2π−β)/m, w=f_m(β)=sinα/sinβ. Positive definiteness of reduced cycle Hessian is exactly cosα+m w cosβ>0, equivalent to f_m′(β)<0. The second derivative of log f_m is strictly positive on (π/2,π), its derivative changes sign exactly once, so there is one fold w_m< w_c; synchrony is the only stable equilibrium for w<=w_m and two reflected stable winding states join for w_m<w<=w_c. At equality wc the ordinary positive edges alone span a path, hence stability persists; the fold has an additional zero mode. The asymptotic tan t*=π+t*, m w_m=sec t*+O(m^-2) follows uniformly at its interior nondegenerate optimum. Independently reconstructed one-weak-link Hessians across N=5..30 corroborate. No unrestricted w>wc classification is claimed.
